editorial:
Spring Break at Lake Victoria turns into a bloodbath when an earthquake cracks open the lake floor and releases a swarm of ancient piranha. The town sheriff, Julie Forester, tries to keep her kids safe while dealing with thousands of partying college students. Meanwhile, a sleazy filmmaker is shooting a wild video on the water. The whole thing is loud, silly, and packed with over-the-top gore. You can tell right away this movie knows exactly what it is and leans hard into the fun.

The cast is surprisingly solid, with Elisabeth Shue and Adam Scott bringing real charm to the chaos. The practical effects and crazy kill scenes are the main attraction, and they deliver big time. On the downside, the story is thin and some jokes fall flat. If you love gory creature features and don't mind cheesy humor, this is a blast. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the piranha attack reaches a peak during the Spring Break party, with massive casualties. Julie and her kids manage to escape the water, but the danger isn't over. A scientist reveals the piranha are just babies, and the adult ones are still out there. The movie ends with a giant piranha leaping out of the water and eating the camera, hinting at a bigger threat to come. It's a wild, shocking finish that leaves you wanting more.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gory creature features and cheesy horror comedies.
